transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I understand we need to hold a coverage huddle for the Advanced Chemistry teacher's upcoming three-day absence next month. Before we can post anything to staff, I'll need to review and approve both the coverage roster and the instructional plan. I believe we have a draft plan that uses a single substitute, regular classroom activities, and the standard make-up-work process — but I'd like to hear from each of you on whether there are any relevant updates or concerns I should know about before I make my decision. Let's start with the department chair.

transcript.text: I need to flag a concern with the draft plan. My department calendar shows that the class's graded chemistry lab practical is scheduled for the second day of the absence, and it cannot be replaced by a worksheet. Department policy requires a chemistry-certified teacher to supervise it. I entered the practical in the department calendar this week, but I had not yet forwarded the calendar note to Ms. Morgan, so she may not have been aware of this when reviewing the draft.

A student in the Advanced Chemistry class has an active seizure action plan that requires an adult trained in seizure response to remain in the classroom during laboratory activities. I confirmed both the seizure action plan and Dr. Lena Park's seizure response training record this week — her training is current — but I have not yet attached either record to the coverage request. Given that Mr. Singh has flagged a graded lab practical scheduled during the absence, this requirement is directly relevant to our coverage plan.

I confirmed this in a family meeting and recorded the request in my counseling file, but I have not yet sent it to the classroom teacher. This student needs a printed make-up packet available before the absence begins, so the standard online make-up process will not work for them.
